title: The Goldman Sachs Group (NYSE:GS) Stock Price Target Lowered at UBS Group - MarketBeat

                                       My Trusted Source On November 2, 2026, GS Finance Corp. filed a Free Writing Prospectus revealing two separate offerings of Buffered Index-Linked Notes connected to the EURO STOXX 50 Index and the S&P 500 Futures Excess Return Index, both anticipated to mature in November 2031. The filing explains that the maturity repayment for each $1,000 face amount depends on the final underlier level compared to the initial level. If the underlier closes above its initial level, investors receive $1,000 plus the product of $1,000, the participation rate, and the underlier return. If the underlier finishes at or below the initial level but remains at or above the buffer level, investors receive $1,000. Should the underlier fall below the buffer level, investors receive $1,000 plus the product of the combined underlier return and buffer amount multiplied by $1,000. The filing warns that investors "could lose a significant portion of the face amount" of their notes. The two tranches differ in their underlying assets. The S&P 500 Futures Excess Return Index tranche (CUSIP 40058MPP7) tracks E-mini S&P 500 futures contracts. The filing notes this index "tracks the performance of E-mini S&P 500 futures contracts, not the S&P 500 Index," and clarifies that "the return on an investment in a futures contract is correlated with, but not the same as, the return on buying and holding the securities underlying such contract." The EURO STOXX 50 tranche (CUSIP 40058MPN2) uses the closing or intra-day level of the EURO STOXX 50 Index on the trade date as its initial underlier level. The filing references a preliminary pricing supplement dated October 30, 2026, along with general terms supplement no. 17,745, an October 2026 S&P 500 Futures Excess Return Index supplement, underlier supplement no. 50, and prospectus documents dated February 14, 2025. Investors are advised to consult these documents for comprehensive details on terms, risks, and credit risk related to GS Finance Corp. and The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. Registration Statement No. 333-284538 covers these offerings. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. is listed on the NYSE under the ticker symbol GS, as noted in the filing. title: Hyundai, Daewoo Lift Profits as GS, DL Slip in Q3 - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
■ Builders Report Mixed Third-Quarter Results
Samsung C&T's construction arm grows both revenue and operating profit
Hyundai and Daewoo post higher operating profit despite falling revenue
GS and DL see declines in both revenue and operating profit South Korea's largest builders extended their earnings recovery in the third quarter, improving profitability even as revenue declined. Low-margin projects launched when construction costs were surging have wound down, and cost-control efforts are paying off. Still, results diverged sharply across companies — hit by shrinking housing volumes and additional costs at overseas plant projects — and analysts say it is too early to call a full industry turnaround. Samsung C&T's (028260.KS) construction division posted revenue of 4.465 trillion won ($3.1 billion) and operating profit of 277 billion won, up 44.5% and 104.5% from a year earlier, according to filings with the Financial Supervisory Service's electronic disclosure system on the 2nd. Both top line and margins improved as high-tech work, including semiconductor plant construction, moved into full swing. Hyundai Engineering & Construction (000720.KS) saw revenue fall 20.3% to 6.2406 trillion won ($4.4 billion), but operating profit rose 114.2% to 221.7 billion won. Daewoo Engineering & Construction (047040.KS) reported revenue of 1.8424 trillion won ($1.3 billion), down 7.4%, while operating profit surged 223.7% to 183.2 billion won. Revenue slipped as the number of active sites fell, but cost management and a profitability-focused approach to project selection translated into stronger earnings, analysts said. GS E&C (006360.KS) and DL E&C (375500.KS), by contrast, continued to struggle. GS E&C posted revenue of 2.7442 trillion won ($1.9 billion) and operating profit of 95.5 billion won, down 14.5% and 35.7% respectively from a year earlier, weighed down by lower housing revenue. DL E&C reported revenue of 1.5065 trillion won ($1.1 billion) and operating profit of 107.3 billion won, down 21.0% and 8.1%. Schedule extensions and additional construction costs booked on the Shaheen project weighed on results. Industry officials say the completion of older low-margin sites and tighter cost controls are lifting profitability, but that this is hard to read as a broad recovery. A drop in new housing starts could leave a revenue gap ahead, and the burden of construction costs and financing expenses remains. Future earnings will hinge less on the sheer size of new orders than on the profitability of the work already secured and how quickly it converts into revenue. Whether improved operating profit feeds through to stronger cash flow and lower borrowings is also seen as a key gauge of builders' financial strength. title: GS E&C data breach exposes blind spots in Korea's smart apartments - The Korea Times
content: GS Engineering & Construction detected unauthorized external access to a system managing apartment community-facility reservations last Wednesday. The incident has raised concerns about the security of digital services used in Korea’s apartment complexes, where residents’ personal and access-related information is collected. The full extent of the exposure remains under investigation, and experts say similar systems used by other builders and public housing operators may also warrant review. When Park, a 56-year-old homemaker living in an apartment complex in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, heard that GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) had recently detected unauthorized access to a system containing residents’ personal information, the news struck a nerve. “Sure, I’ve had my personal information exposed in the Coupang and SK Telecom data breaches, among many others. Over time, I found myself becoming less concerned. Everyone seemed to be getting hit, and it felt like I was just another number in a database,” she said. This time, however, it felt much closer to home, quite literally. “The information involved could reveal details about my own household. Our apartment complex, like many newer developments, relies on smart home services for everyday tasks. We use an app to track package deliveries and vehicle entry and exit, another to access the building, and I hear the sports center is introducing facial recognition for entry. If that kind of information gets exposed, it feels like someone might actually be able to track my every move.” Her concerns point to a growing vulnerability in a country where apartment living and digital technology are increasingly intertwined. Apartments account for a staggering 65.8 percent of all homes in Korea, according to 2025 data from the Ministry of Data and Statistics. As residential complexes adopt digital systems for everything from identity verification and building access to household device controls, they are also collecting more detailed information about residents and their routines. The security implications came into focus last Wednesday, when GS E&C said it had detected unauthorized external access to a system used to manage reservations for apartment community facilities. The potentially exposed data goes beyond basic identifying details, such as residents’ names, dates of birth and contact information. It also includes information about their residential status, whether they are the head of their household and radio-frequency identification (RFID) card numbers. Passwords were also listed among the affected information, although the company said they were encrypted. The full extent of the exposure remains under investigation. A panoramic view of apartment complexes in Seoul's Seongbuk District, Sunday / Yonhap Over the years, major construction companies have expanded their digital services for residents, offering platforms that combine smart home controls with building access, visitor registration and reservations for shared facilities. GS E&C operates its “Xi Home” platform, while Hyundai Engineering & Construction, Samsung C&T and Daewoo Engineering & Construction offer similar services across their apartment complexes. As these services have proliferated, however, information security may not have kept pace with the expansion, experts say, as construction has traditionally been viewed as a building-focused sector. The risks extend beyond the exposure of personal identifiers. RFID card numbers can be linked to systems controlling access to apartment buildings and shared facilities, while some complexes are starting to use facial recognition and other biometric data for entry. “RFID cards are used to control access to apartment buildings and shared facilities like saunas and gyms,” said Youm Heung-youl, an emeritus professor of information security at Soonchunhyang University. “The risks are even greater with facial recognition. Although there is no indication that biometric information was compromised in the GS E&C incident, its exposure could create further privacy risks, including the potential misuse of facial data in AI (artificial intelligence)-generated images.” The potential impact could also extend beyond a single apartment complex. “This is unlikely to be a problem limited to GS E&C. Other construction companies and public housing operators use similar systems. If multiple apartment complexes share a platform, a breach affecting one complex could spread to others. We need to examine whether these platforms are being managed securely,” he said. The professor called for a broader review of vulnerabilities in apartment management systems and their connections to external networks, noting that existing safeguards — including certified Internet of Things devices and separation between internal and shared networks — may not be sufficient.

title: GS E&C Develops 20 Standard Steel Modular Floor Plans - Seoul Economic Daily
content: GS E&C (006360.KS) said on the 2nd that it has developed 20 standard steel modular floor plans for use in apartments, officetels (studio-style units in mixed-use residential-commercial buildings), hotels and dormitories, and linked them to construction-cost estimation technology based on building information modeling (BIM). Steel modular construction involves prefabricating major structural components and finishes at a factory and assembling them on site. The method shortens construction schedules and makes quality control easier, but it requires design work and cost reviews tailored to modular characteristics in the early stages of a project, making it difficult for clients to assess feasibility. To reduce that burden, GS E&C developed standard floor plans for a range of uses and equipped them with layouts, 3D models and interior renderings so clients can compare and review suitable products without a separate initial design process. The standard plans widen the bay configuration compared with earlier designs to create a more open feel, and they can propose how modules should be arranged not only within individual units but also around the core — the stairwell and elevator space — of an entire building. Apartments and officetels were designed as compact residential products that balance space efficiency and livability, while the hotel plans cover room types ranging from business-class to luxury and residence-grade. By linking the standard plans with BIM models, the company said, it can quickly calculate expected construction costs for a given design, helping clients decide efficiently whether to proceed with a project. To broaden use of the standard products, GS E&C also built a Steel Modular Standard Floor Plan Portal, where layouts, 3D models and interior renderings matched to specific uses and project sizes can be viewed at a glance. The company is pursuing design registrations for the standard plans to secure intellectual property rights, and next year it plans to work with Korea Land & Housing Corporation (LH) to extend the lineup to residential plans of 65 and 75 square meters. "The significance of these standard floor plans is that they let clients choose a suitable design from the earliest stage of a project and quickly review construction costs and feasibility," a GS E&C official said. "We will continue to advance our standard products and the technology linking design with cost estimates to support rational decision-making by clients and strengthen the competitiveness of our modular business." Ex-FIFA GS Joins Historic Celebration as Africa Welcomes First Youth Olympic Games Former FIFA Secretary General Fatma Samba Diouf Samoura joined the final procession of Olympic Flame bearers in Dakar ahead of the official opening ceremony of the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, marking a significant moment in Senegal’s preparations to host the first Olympic event on African soil, BSNSports.com.ng reports. Samoura participated in the final leg of the relay alongside international personalities, including Senegalese social media star Khaby Lame, actor Omar Sy, wrestling champion Modou Lô and other prominent figures from  sports, entertainment and public life.Sports news subscription The final procession, held in a celebratory atmosphere in Dakar, brought together athletes, artists and residents to celebrate the Olympic spirit and the role of African youth in shaping the continent’s future. The Olympic Flame, which originated in Athens, travelled across Senegal for 47 days, covering more than 3,650 kilometres from Dakar to Ziguinchor and back to the capital. The nationwide relay passed through Thiès, Saint-Louis, Matam, Kaolack, Tambacounda, Kédougou and Kolda, among other locations, covering all 14 regions of the country. Approximately 450 torchbearers participated in more than 30 stages of the relay, which also featured sporting, cultural and educational activities designed to engage young people and local communities. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games represent a historic breakthrough for Africa, as Senegal becomes the first African country to host an Olympic event. The Games mark a new chapter in the history of the Olympic movement, providing a global platform to showcase Africa’s sporting potential, cultural diversity and youthful population. Organisers expect approximately 2,700 athletes to compete across around 20 sporting disciplines, with the event being celebrated under the motto, "Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates." The hosting of the Games is also expected to strengthen Africa’s position in international sport while creating opportunities for young athletes to demonstrate their talents on a global stage. Samoura’s participation in the final torch relay reflects her longstanding contribution to international sports administration and development. A Senegalese national, she spent more than two decades working with the United Nations, holding senior positions in humanitarian affairs and development across several continents. In 2016, she made history when she was appointed FIFA Secretary General, becoming the first woman and the first African to occupy the position. She served in the role until 2023, overseeing the federation’s administration and contributing to the organisation of several FIFA World Cups. During her tenure, she also supported initiatives aimed at expanding football development, particularly women's football, while promoting improved governance and modernisation within the global football governing body. Following her departure from FIFA, Samoura has continued her involvement in international sports and development initiatives. She is currently a member of the FIA Senate and serves on the boards of organisations including Seed Project and African Collaborations Group (ACG). Her participation in the final Olympic Flame relay symbolised the connection between her experience in global sports administration and Africa’s growing ambitions on the international sporting stage. "To carry the flame is to carry a dream, and to pass it on is to pass on its energy," Samoura said. The final Olympic Flame relay preceded the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which took place on October 31 at the Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio. The ceremony was attended by Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye, International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Kirsty Coventry, Dakar 2026 Organising Committee President Mamadou Diagna Ndiaye and sports ministers representing African countries. The ceremony officially launched the first Youth Olympic Games to be staged on the African continent, placing Senegal at the centre of a historic moment for African sport. For Samoura and other prominent personalities who participated in the Flame relay, the occasion represented more than a ceremonial celebration. title: GS E&C standardizes steel modular layouts, links BIM to speed cost decisions - Chosunbiz
content: Standard floor plans and BIM-linked estimates aim to speed early feasibility checks for modular builds GS Engineering & Construction has developed standard floor plans for steel modular construction and will apply them to its building business. GS Engineering & Construction said on the 2nd it has developed 20 types of steel modular standard floor plans that can be applied to a range of uses, including apartments, officetels, hotels, and dormitories, and will link them to construction cost estimation based on building information modeling (BIM) to support customers' swift feasibility reviews. The development focuses on enabling customers to select designs suited to the intended use and size and to review expected construction costs from the early stage of a project. It streamlines the design and estimate review process that used to be carried out for each project, helping decision-making needed to推进 modular projects. Steel modular is a building method in which major structural elements and finishes are manufactured in a factory and then assembled on-site. While it has strengths in shortening construction duration and quality control, in the early stage of a project it requires design and cost reviews that reflect modular characteristics, which has made it difficult for customers to judge feasibility. To reduce this burden, GS Engineering & Construction developed standard floor plans for various uses based on its accumulated residential design experience and modular production know-how. With floor plans, 3D models, and interior renderings in place, customers can compare and review products suited to their project conditions without a separate initial design process. The new standard floor plans are characterized by standardized module specifications and configurations that allow for various combinations. By expanding the bay configuration compared with existing plans, they enhance a sense of openness in the space, and they can also propose how to place each module around the building's core (stair and elevator space) for an entire wing, not just individual units. Apartments and officetels are configured as compact residential products with space efficiency and living convenience in mind. For hotels, a range of room types is provided from business grade to luxury and residence grade, and the product lineup has been diversified so it can also be applied to dormitories, youth housing, and military quarters. In particular, by linking the standard floor plans with BIM models, expected construction costs can be quickly calculated according to each design option. Customers can compare floor plans and building layout alternatives and review construction costs from the early stage of a project, enabling efficient decisions on whether to proceed. GS Engineering & Construction also built a "steel modular standard floor plan portal" to increase the usability of the standard products. It plans to use it for design consultations with customers and project reviews by allowing users to see floor plans, 3D models, and interior renderings suited to the intended use and size at a glance. In addition, the company will pursue design registrations for the standard floor plans to secure intellectual property (IP), and next year, in partnership with LH, it will expand development to medium and large residential floor plans of 65㎡ and 75㎡ to strengthen product competitiveness. Nazrul Islam, head of public affairs and brand communication at Dutch-Bangla Bank, has been elected general secretary. The new leadership was announced on Friday at a get-together organised by Daily Bonik Barta at a hotel in Gulshan, Dhaka, according to a press release. Founded in 2011 by professionals working in the branding and communication departments of the country’s banks, PRAB is governed by a 33-member executive committee, which serves a two-year term. Heads of public relations and branding departments of leading commercial banks, along with senior public relations officials of Bangladesh Bank, serve in various positions on the committee. Moniruzzaman Tipu, founding general secretary of PRAB, announced the names of the new leaders. Yet a valuation approach built on the returns the firm generates on its capital suggests the stock may still trade below what those returns support. High-profile deal activity, including a planned listing from a prominent AI developer, adds to the story. The question is whether this rally still has room to run. Goldman Sachs is a leading global financial institution offering advisory, underwriting, trading, asset management, and wealth management services to corporations, governments, institutions, and individuals. The firm plays a central role in mergers, capital raising, and market-making across stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodities. As a closely watched  financial stock, Goldman Sachs is often viewed as a barometer of dealmaking activity and capital markets health worldwide. Goldman Sachs' stock has delivered an exceptional rally over the past few years, multiplying in value as dealmaking revived, trading desks thrived, and the firm sharpened its focus on core strengths. A run of that size naturally raises questions about whether the price has outpaced the underlying business. Answering that question requires looking beyond the chart to the returns the firm generates on the capital owners have entrusted to it. One useful way to value a bank is to compare the return it generates on equity with its cost of equity, which represents the return owners require for taking on risk. When a bank consistently produces returns above that cost, it creates value beyond its book value. Goldman Sachs' average return on equity sits well above its estimated cost of equity, indicating that each dollar of owner capital is producing a meaningful surplus. An excess returns model builds on that idea by estimating the surplus Goldman Sachs generates above its cost of equity and projecting how long that surplus can last. The model starts from the firm's current book value and a stable book value estimate, then applies its average return on equity. Because the surplus is treated as durable rather than a one-off, the model assigns it meaningful economic value in calculating the firm's intrinsic worth. Under this excess returns approach, Goldman Sachs' estimated intrinsic value sits meaningfully above its current stock price. That implies the market is pricing the firm at a discount to what its returns on equity and capital distributions support. In other words, despite the long rally, the stock may not fully reflect the firm's ability to generate surplus returns. The stock also trades at a moderate price-to-earnings multiple. Goldman Sachs' strong returns reflect healthy  earnings per share growth supported by booming trading activity, recovering deal volumes, and expanding wealth and asset management businesses. Equities trading has been especially robust as hedge funds and institutional clients increased activity. That combination of diversified revenue streams helps the firm sustain high returns on equity across different market environments. A separate dividend lens adds support to the valuation case. Goldman Sachs pays a steady dividend, and its  dividend yield reflects a payout that uses only a modest portion of bottom-line results. The valuation model assumes long-term dividend growth at a capped, conservative rate, treating the stream of distributions as both ongoing and growing. That reliable income adds another layer of value for long-term owners. Goldman Sachs is closely tied to high-profile transactions, including a planned initial public offering from a prominent AI developer and several large merger deals. Advisory and underwriting roles on marquee transactions generate significant fees and reinforce the firm's reputation. How consistently Goldman converts these strengths into durable returns on equity will shape whether its current valuation discount persists or narrows over time. The key assumption behind the excess returns view is that Goldman's surplus returns can last. Dealmaking and trading are cyclical, and periods of market stress can compress returns quickly. Still, the firm's diversified business, global client base, and leadership in advisory work have historically helped it recover from downturns. Sustained returns above its cost of equity would support the case that the stock remains undervalued. The clearest risk is that dealmaking or trading activity slows, reducing returns on equity and weakening the valuation case. Market volatility could pressure trading revenue. Stricter capital rules may limit capital returns to owners. Competition from other global banks remains intense. And after a powerful multiyear rally, the stock could pull back if returns fail to meet elevated expectations. Return on equity trends will be the most important indicator to watch, revealing whether the firm sustains surplus returns. Deal activity, including major listings and mergers, will show advisory momentum. Trading revenue will reflect market conditions. Dividend growth will indicate confidence in cash generation. title: Becky G might be the all-time best gift-giver — these are her top picks for this holiday season - NBC News
content: Becky G doesn’t play around with holiday gifts — here’s what she’s giving the lucky people in her life this season NBC Selected independently determines what we cover and recommend. When you click on or buy through our links, we earn a commission. Learn more. Talking Shop is our series where we talk to interesting people about their most interesting buys. Becky G has been going nonstop all year. Not only did the singer release her fifth studio album, Baraja Bendita, which was nominated for Top Latin Pop Album of the Year at the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards, but she also filmed a new movie and led a cross-country headlining tour. She also helped Patrón design a limited-edition “Our Rainwater Project” bottle, which funded 200 rainwater harvesting systems for households in Jalisco, Mexico. Needless to say, the L.A.-based superstar is ready for some much-needed rest and relaxation this holiday season. “I’ve been away from home a lot more this year. I’ve definitely been putting my head down and grinding it out, so I’m looking forward to family time — celebrating with them, reconnecting, and eating some yummy food,” says Becky G. “It’ll be a fun holiday, for sure.” In addition to making her family’s annual tamales, she’s preparing for Las Posadas, a nine-day religious celebration that takes place from December 16 to December 24, and readying her holiday shopping list. “I’m really big on gift giving,” she says. “It’s my favorite time of the year to catch up with everybody and give them things that I’ve put a lot of thought into.” She adds that, regardless of presents and parties, showing up and celebrating together is the most important part of the holiday season. “Now more than ever, there’s a unity that we need as a community and a time that we need with our family. It’s a beautiful reminder of what really matters in life.” Below, Becky G breaks down the gifts on her holiday shopping list this year, including a white elephant gift everyone will fight over and useful stocking stuffers. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Becky G describes herself as ritualistic when it comes to her pre-show routines — and restocks of her go-to essentials are always appreciated around the holidays. “I always have to have palo santo and sage,” she says. “I’m really big on essence sprays and things that cleanse the space. It’s very helpful for me to set the vibes. I’m a vibe curator, so I would say those are things that I absolutely love receiving.” Lé Trois Apothecary offers three essential oil ritual cleansers: one for relaxation and release, one for manifestation, and one for grounding. The brand’s No. 3 cleanser to create unity and connection was inspired by Becky G and it features notes of bergamot, oud, and vetiver. Not one to miss her family’s white elephant gift exchange, Becky G says a bottle of Patrón Tequila was one of the best presents she’s ever brought. “It was the hot ticket item that everybody was battling it out for, and at the end, people started linking up with other people to trade gifts to get it.” An official partner of the brand, she recently designed an exclusive bottle for the Rainwater Project, which helped bring 200 rainwater harvesting systems to families in Jalisco, Mexico. A fan of buying and gifting things with intention, Becky G is planning on giving friends a bottle from that collection this year because it’s a present that’s connected to something close to her heart. “When I’ve been given things that are for the community and for the culture, it hits me differently and it reminds me that we’re a part of something bigger and it makes me want to do the same,” she says. Patrón silver tequila is an unaged blanco tequila made from 100% Weber Blue Agave. You must be 21+ to purchase and consume. If someone came up to Becky G and asked her for a mid-luxury beauty product to give as a gift, she’d recommend Dezi Skin’s Agua Fresca Moisturizer. “Desi Perkins killed it with Dezi Skin; there’s not one product that I do not love, especially Pore Choices, the new mist she just released. But, the OG Agua Fresca moisturizer is also incredible,” she says. The fragrance-free gel-cream moisturizer is formulated with niacinamide, hyaluronic acid and antioxidants to help give skin a much-needed boost of hydration. It’s lightweight and can be used with all skin types to help target fine lines, dryness and elasticity. Every year, Becky G likes to give her team presents that they can make together. Last year, she bought them a Mexican coffee set from a small cafe in Los Angeles. The kit included the coffeehouse’s signature Café de Olla — a traditional Mexican coffee brewed with ground cinnamon and piloncillo (unrefined Mexican sugar) — and a bag of Oaxaca Reserve beans. “Little thoughtful things like that are super, super fun to put together,” she says. Traditionally, café de olla is made in a clay pot, which imbues the coffee with more flavor. While you can make café de olla in a regular saucepan, you can also purchase an olla for less than $40 on Etsy — just make sure to wash it by hand with warm water and baking soda (or coarse salt) when you’re done. Chemical-based detergents are easily absorbed into the clay and can give your food (and coffee) a soapy taste. One thing about Becky G is she commits to an aesthetic. Each of her family members gets a matching color scheme for the holidays that’s themed to their personalities, which she helps curate on Etsy. “I get down on wrapping presents. That’s the one thing I enjoy,” she says, noting that she’s usually the one going around and saving the tissue paper and unripped bags. “There’s some bags that have been around at my Christmas for eight years now. We can’t just use these once, come on.” As someone who’s always traveling, Becky G loves tin candles, and she thinks they make a great addition to any stocking. “Tin candles help make a room feel a little more custom to your vibe,” she says. “They’re usually a little bit more potent in scent, so you don’t need to leave them [burning] for a very long time.” During the holidays, she opts for scents like apple cinnamon, which she says reminds her of her mom’s house, and pine. One of her go-to candle brands is Soy Latina Candles, a non-toxic soy candle brand that offers scents inspired by the owner’s Latina heritage. Another of Becky G’s go-to stocking stuffer ideas is anything practical that can be kept in a glove box, like individually packed hand wipes, silk hair ties and lip balm. “I be doing too much with the stockings sometimes. I’m like, it’s overflowing at this point,” she says. I’m a newsletter editor at NBC Selected. title: +100 kg: Demetrashvili Gets it All Right in Abu Dhabi - IJF
content: Final: Ushangi Kokauri (AZE) vs Irakli Demetrashvili (GEO) This was an entertaining contest with both judoka focused on finding that one all-important score that would carry them to the top of the podium. There can only be one winner though and in this case it was Irakli Demetrashvili who tipped the balance. The Georgian judoka put together a neat combination to throw his Azerbaijani opponent, transitioning to osaekomi to seal the deal. An impressive silver medal has been earned in Abu Dhabi by Ushangi Kokauri on the back of his world championship success, while Irakli Demetrashvili claims a superb gold medal to add to his growing collection. “After missing a medal at the World Championships in Baku, I improved my condition and am thrilled to become a double grand slam gold medallist.” Irakli Demetrashvili was happy to be interviewed after the final. “Winning in Tbilisi and adding several medals to my list this season has been very satisfying. Training with legends like Lasha Shavdatuashvili teaches me valuable lessons, as every win or loss provides details to analyse and improve step-by-step. While I am happy with my progress, I am also looking ahead to events like the Tokyo Grand Slam, but I won't be fully satisfied until I win a world championship gold medal.” Bronze medal contest: Denis Batchaev (RUS) vs Giannis Antoniou (CYP) Giannis Antoniou struggled to keep up with the energy presented to him by Denis Batchaev, the latter leading the gripping and the movement convincingly. Although Batchaev wasn’t able to score in tachi-waza, he hunted scores on the ground too and claimed an ippon win with an armlock, a situation Antoniou could not escape from. Bronze medal contest: Martti Puumalainen (FIN) vs Saba Inaneishvili (GEO) Martti Puumalainen seemed unable to get into the fight, looking out of sorts from the beginning. Saba Inaneishvili, on the other hand, was super-mobile and made space to catch Puumalainen with a neat ashi-waza at the halfway point. From there, the time ticked away and Inaneishvili could be satisfied with his medal-winning performance in Abu Dhabi. 31. Oct. 2026 / This edition of the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam has concluded ... 31. title: -100 kg: Bifov Climbs to the Top of the Podium - IJF
content: This was an explosive contest that looked to be heading France’s way. Aurelien Diesse had energy and dynamic movement and he seemed unfired to attack. He scored a yuko after 90 seconds had passed but during the same exchange, Bifov took the advantage and turned a deficit into a win, armlocking Diesse. From his place at 129th in the world ranking, Diesse can be proud of his new sil ver medal but the crown is Bifov’s today, his second grand slam gold. After the final, Idar Bifov said, “I feel joy and happiness. The first bout was harder than the final but I managed to win the gold medal this year in Abu Dhabi, just like last year. Before the final, we analysed the Frenchman's previous match and my coach helped me prepare, pointeing out the mistakes I needed to avoid.” Bronze medal contest: Zsombor Veg (HUN) vs Anton Savytskiy (UKR) Zsombor Veg had a fantastic morning session and looked to be working with momentum in the final block, but for a single moment of inspire judo from Anton Savytskiy who launched a seoi-otoshi under him to score a yuko just 37 seconds before the end of the contest. Unable to make up the shortfall in such a short time, Veg had to settle for 5th place. Anton Savytskiy now has his ninth World Judo Tour medal, a career that is really beginning to take shape. Bronze medal contest: Marat Baikamurov (KAZ) vs Adam Sangariev (RUS) This was another close contest for all of the normal period, just a couple of penalties were visible on the board. However, in golden score, Marat Baikamurov opened up and found his way into a winning position, scoring a yuko that earned him the medal. This is his third grand slam medal. 31. title: +78 kg: Victory for Vukovic - IJF
content: Helena Vukovic gripped excellently to neutralise Hershko’s usual attacks but Raz has other strings to her bow. She began to mix up the techniques, adding ashi-waza to the mix and coming close to taking a lead just a minute before the end. Vukovic escaped, just, and so the stalemate, albeit a dynamic one, continued. Vukovic made the most of the additional time afforded to them in golden score. She raised the pace and attacked more frequently, forcing penalties against Hershko which eventually totalled three, signifying the end of the contest. Hershko, the favourite, had a new silver medal, while Helena Vukovic, having played an excellent strategy, had her first grand slam gold medal. “I’m feeling really happy with my first grand slam gold medal, especially after getting my first win over an amazing opponent, staying focused and executing our tactics,” said Helena Vukovic. “It lifts a huge weight off my shoulders to start my Olympic qualification with such a strong result. I always love competing in Abu Dhabi and I'm super excited to head to Zagreb next for the grand prix, to perform in front of our incredibly supportive home crowd.” Bronze medal contest: Giovanna Santos (BRA) vs Asya Tavano (ITA) With Italy hunting two bronze medals, each of their final block competitors was keen not to fall behind. Asya tavano began very well, resisting an attack from Giovanna Santos and transitioning directly into an osaekomi situation. She held her opponent for the full 20 seconds to earn a solid win and a new World Judo Tour medal. Bronze medal contest: Madina Kaisinova (AZE) vs Erica Simonetti (ITA) Simonetti began with a high pace, a difficult opponent to slow down. She built momentum and scored twice, a yuko each time, the first from a well placed seoi-otoshi. Having seen her teammate win the first bronze medal of the category, additional motivation drove her through the remaining time and she defended perfectly, remaining positive throughout. Italy takes two beronze medals in this group as well as one at -90 kg; a very good day indeed. 31. Oct. 2026 / This edition of the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam has concluded ... 31. title: -78 kg: Lytvynenko Leads Again - IJF
content: FInal: Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko (UAE) vs Patricia Sampaio (POR) The world number two and world number five delivered an exceptionally high level final, one that was balancing on a knife edge. With either judoka poised to claim the win at any moment, furious attacks coming from white and blue, the volume rose in the Mubadala Arena. After two minutes of extra time Sampaio had two penalties and Lytvynenko had one but there were spells of dominance from both. However, a minute later, Sampaio attacked with a seoi-otoshi that lacked a little movement and Lytvynenko capitalised, countering for a waza-ari and the gold. This is a perfect finish for the host nation, a gold medal on the third and final day of competition in Abu Dhabi. “I feel good, said Lytvynenko, “I’m tired but I'm happy because it feels like home and I am so glad to win a gold medal for my country. It was tough coming straight from the World Championships with such a short turnaround, especially after my training camp in Baku but we are here and we took the gold medal. My opponent is a very good fighter with strong techniques. It's a very good feeling to fight here and this is very important for our team.” Bronze medal contest: Karol Gimenes (BRA) vs Yael Van Heemst (NED) This was a game of judo chess from the outset, each competitor searching for the right movement and grip to unbalance the other. For 3 minutes and 59 seconds, all was even but active and fate was calling for extra time. However, Yael Van Heemst was not waiting for the gong and turned in, in the very last moment to score as the clocked reached four minutes. Bronze medal contest: Metka Lotnik (SLO) vs Emma Reid (GBR) For four minutes Emma Reid of Great Britain looked to be edging the contest but nothing on the scoreboard separated them, meaning some extra time was required. A minute into golden score, exactly a minute, Reid worked through a transition phase perfectly to secure a juji-gatame. “Ippon” was called and Reid showed her satisfaction for a job well done. 31. title: Karnataka Rajyotsava Award row: Outrage over withdrawal of Dr G S Chandrashekar’s name - Daijiworld
content:
GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS TITLE ATTEMPT - Day 1 Udupi, Oct 31: The Karnataka government's decision to withdraw the Rajyotsava Award announced for renowned Udupi-based physician Dr G S Chandrashekar has sparked widespread criticism, with citizens, medical professionals and various organisations expressing strong displeasure over the move. Dr G S Chandrashekar, medical director of Udupi's reputed Adarsha Hospital, was initially named among the recipients of this year's Karnataka Rajyotsava Awards. However, in a subsequent development, his name was removed from the list, reportedly citing technical reasons. The decision has come as a shock to many in Udupi, particularly considering Dr Chandrashekar's contributions to the healthcare sector. He has dedicated more than three decades to providing selfless medical services to the people of Udupi and has earned widespread recognition for his commitment to patient care and public service. The government's move has raised questions over the selection process, with many questioning why an award was announced in the first place if there were technical issues that warranted his exclusion. Adding to the controversy, the government had announced a Rajyotsava Award recipient from Uttara Kannada district, while Dr Chandrashekar's name from Udupi was subsequently withdrawn. The decision has triggered strong reactions from the medical fraternity, various organisations and members of the public, who have expressed disappointment and demanded clarity from the state government. Many believe that Dr Chandrashekar's decades-long contribution to society deserves recognition and have urged the government to reconsider its decision. Dr P V Bhandary questions withdrawal, seeks reinstatement of award In a statement, Dr P V Bhandary, renowned psychiatrist and social worker of Udupi said that the issue was merely a district-name error and could have been corrected through a simple amendment rather than withdrawing the award altogether. Recalling his professional association with Dr Chandrashekar during their service at a government hospital, Dr Bhandary said he had personally witnessed the latter's commitment to medical service. He pointed out that Dr Chandrashekar has been responding to emergency calls at any hour, irrespective of a patient's identity or financial background, and has continued such selfless service for nearly three decades. "An administrative mistake should be corrected by the concerned department. A person who has done no wrong should not have to pay the price for it," Dr Bhandary stated. Clarifying that he had no objection to the selection of G U Bhat, whose name was subsequently included in the award list, Dr Bhandary said his appeal was solely to ensure justice for Dr Chandrashekar. He urged the Karnataka and Udupi branches of the Indian Medical Association (IMA) to submit an official protest to the government. He also appealed to the chief minister and the department of Kannada and Culture to reinstate the Rajyotsava Award announced for Dr Chandrashekar, with Udupi district correctly mentioned. Dr G S Chandrashekar is the right person, government should correct its mistake - Ansar Ahmed Speaking exclusively with Daijiworld.com Ansar Ahmed, a social worker, stated, "Dr G S Chandrashekar is the right person for the Rajyotsava Award." It is a shame for the government to announce the award and then again to take it back. Dr G S Chandrashekar has rendered selfless service for the district for over 30 years. He is the only person who would overcome any difficulty and render his service even at 12 am if required. I have witnessed his selfless service in many occasions. It was the government's mistake, and the government should correct it themselves. I urge the state government to reinstate the award declared for Dr G S Chandrashekar. It is a dishonour done to the professional healthcare community." Meanwhile, Umesh A Naik of Cherkady has also strongly criticised the government's decision, stating that such an irresponsible decision does not bring credit to the administration. In his statement, Umesh Naik described Adarsha Hospital as a reputed healthcare institution in Udupi district and highlighted Dr Chandrashekar's contributions to medical and social service for over 30 years. He said the institution has been a source of hope for the underprivileged through its continued healthcare and social initiatives. He termed the decision to announce Dr Chandrashekar's name for the prestigious award and subsequently remove it citing a technical error as unfortunate and unjustified. Withdrawing an award after its announcement amounts to an insult not only to the individual concerned but also to the wider community that recognises and respects his contributions, he said. Umesh Naik urged the state government to take the matter seriously, rectify the injustice and re-announce the Rajyotsava Award in Dr Chandrashekar's name in recognition of his longstanding service. The demand for reinstating the award has gained attention in Udupi, with calls growing for the government to correct the alleged administrative error and recognise Dr Chandrashekar's three decades of dedicated service. title: Hi-Pass' Kim Debuts Against GS Caltex in Season Opener - 조선일보
content: New coach aims to build resilient team after past losses to defending champions [Jangchung=Sports Chosun Reporter Lee Jong-seo] "I'm very nervous." Korea Expressway Corporation Hi-Pass will play its opening match against HK Heungkuk Financial 2026–2027 V-League Women's Division GS Caltex at Jangchung Gymnasium on the 31st. Two days before the opening. The Expressway Corporation appointed acting coach Kim Young-rae as the official head coach. Before last year's championship finals, the Expressway Corporation announced a split with head coach Kim Jong-min and handed the reins to then-chief coach Kim Young-rae. After losing to GS Caltex in the championship finals, the team successfully advanced to the finals of the cup tournament. However, they were once again defeated by GS Caltex, leaving them with regret. Nevertheless, Kim, who was highly praised for stabilizing and leading the team, was officially appointed as head coach. Coach Kim, who will make his debut as official head coach on the 31st, said, "I'm very nervous. I'm also excited. I've prepared well, so I want to help the players do their best." Comparing his previous role as acting coach to his current position, Kim stated, "Being the official head coach is much more nerve-wracking. The first button is the most important. It's the start of the season and my first time as a head coach. I'm very nervous, but I trust the players." Regarding his volleyball philosophy, he emphasized, "We must avoid unforced errors. If players are not in position and fail to set the ball, it dampens the team's morale. I've talked a lot about this. I hope the team never gives up. My biggest challenge is to build a team that fans see as passionate and tenacious on the court." To win the debut match, they must overcome the 'defending champions' GS Caltex. Kim revealed, "We didn't lose because we couldn't stop Silva; we failed to block domestic players. Strengthening our blocking seems right." GS Caltex head coach Lee Young-taek said, "Kim Young-rae is a close junior I played with during my career. His first match as acting coach was also against us. It feels fateful that our first match as official coaches is again against each other. The Expressway Corporation is a well-organized and solid team. I expect a tough game. We won our last match (in the cup tournament) and are on a good streak. I hope our players show their best on the court, like in the finals."

title: 2024 BMW F 900 GS Buyer’s Guide [Specs, Price] - Ultimate Motorcycling
content: The 2024 BMW F 900 GS replaces the F 850 GS and turns the middleweight GS into a more off-road-capable adventure bike, while the new F 800 GS takes over the street-focused role. The F 900 GS weighs 31 pounds less than the 850, much of it trimmed high or far from the center of gravity. The 3.8-gallon plastic fuel tank alone is 10 pounds lighter than the old steel tank, and the rear subframe, Akrapovič muffler, and LED headlight are lighter, too. Curb weight is 483 pounds. A handlebar raised 0.6 inches, footpegs lowered 0.8 inches, and a slimmer tank and tail make the GS feel like a big dirt bike when standing. The 34.3-inch seat height is tall; optional Rallye seats lower it 1.4 inches or raise it 0.8 inches. The 895cc parallel twin from the F 900 R and F 900 XR makes 105 horsepower and 69 ft-lbs of torque, 10 horsepower more than the 850. A 270/450-degree firing order gives it a pleasant throb instead of a buzz, and the GS is stable and comfortable on long freeway stints. A fully adjustable 43mm Showa inverted fork and a ZF shock with rebound damping and hydraulic spring-preload adjustment provide about nine inches of travel at each end. The suspension is compliant without being soft and stays balanced off-road. The $1495 Enduro Package Pro adds a fully adjustable 45mm Showa fork, a fully adjustable Sachs ZF shock, and a taller handlebar. Twin 305mm front discs with two-piston Brembo calipers have a soft initial bite that suits the dirt. Road and Rain ride modes are standard. The $1750 Premium Package adds Dynamic, Enduro, and Enduro Pro modes, a quickshifter, cruise control, keyless ride, GPS prep, and tire-pressure monitoring. Enduro Pro is the dirt mode, with strong, linear throttle response, minimal traction control, and front-only ABS.
